footer.tagline: Workforce scheduling for shift- & field-based operations
cta.openSourceNote: Klacks is open source under the AGPL-3.0. Host it yourself, keep your data in-house, pay no license fees — you stay in full control.
cta.demoResetNote: The Playground is a public Klacks instance, not a production system. Explore Klacks with sample data; all data is reset daily. Klacksy uses external AI providers here — do not enter real personal data.
demoModal.title: Heads up: the Playground is public
demoModal.body: The Playground is only for trying things out and playing around — it is not a production installation. All data is periodically reset. The AI assistant Klacksy uses external AI providers here — do not enter real personal data. In your own installation you choose the AI model yourself, including a local one.
demoModal.languageNote: The default language is German. You can switch the language in the app under Profile.
routePlanning.title: The best route — automatically
routePlanning.subtitle: From your service addresses, Klacks works out the most sensible order and shows the finished route on the map. All you choose is the mode of transport.
routePlanning.step1Text: Every service location has an address on file — Klacks knows the way.
routePlanning.step2Text: Klacks works out the shortest sensible sequence — detours and empty runs disappear.
routePlanning.step3Text: The finished route appears on the map — by car, bike, or on foot.
routePlanning.mapCaption: Stylized example: Klacks connects the service locations into the shortest route.
notFound.title: This page doesn’t exist.
notFound.text: The address doesn’t exist or has moved. Perhaps there’s a typo — or you followed an outdated link.
ruleOps.title: Rule violations: Klacks warns you instantly
ruleOps.subtitle: Real recordings from Klacks with demo data: Klacks flags time collisions, rest periods that are too short, too many consecutive working days and work on holidays right as you plan — as an error or warning in the error list.
ruleConflictDemo.title: Rest period too short
ruleConflictDemo.videoLabel: Video: Klacks warns about a rest period that is too short
ruleConflictDemo.caption: An early shift is assigned to someone who worked a late shift until 10 p.m. the day before — Klacks immediately shows a warning because the configured 11-hour rest period shrinks to 9 hours.
ruleCollisionDemo.title: Time collision
ruleCollisionDemo.videoLabel: Video: Klacks flags a time collision as an error
ruleCollisionDemo.caption: A client appointment is assigned to someone who already has a day shift at the same time — Klacks saves it, but immediately marks the overlap in red as an error in the error list.
ruleConsecutiveDaysDemo.title: Too many days in a row
ruleConsecutiveDaysDemo.videoLabel: Video: Klacks warns about too many consecutive working days
ruleConsecutiveDaysDemo.caption: Three early shifts move over to someone who already has four shifts this week — Klacks keeps count: first the week’s second rest day goes missing, then the seventh consecutive working day brings a second warning.
ruleHolidayWorkDemo.title: Work on a holiday
ruleHolidayWorkDemo.videoLabel: Video: Klacks warns about work on a statutory holiday
ruleHolidayWorkDemo.caption: A day shift is placed on 25 December — Klacks knows the regional holiday calendar and flags the holiday work as a warning before anyone overlooks it.
klacksyPlansWeek.videoLabel: Video: Klacksy starts the weekly planning
klacksyPlansWeek.caption: Real recording from Klacks with demo data: in the chat, Klacksy starts the planning assistant for one week, shows the result and applies it once you confirm — the schedule fills up. Waiting times are shortened.
klacksyOps.title: Klacksy handles this in the chat
klacksyOps.subtitle: Real recordings from Klacks with demo data: you tell Klacksy what to do — Klacksy shows a preview first and applies it only after you confirm.
klacksyOps.videoNote: Waiting times in the video are shortened and marked. How quickly Klacksy responds depends on the chosen AI model; depending on the size of your business, the planning engine takes a few minutes to calculate.
klacksyPlansWeek.title: Plan a week
klacksyGroupsAddress.title: Groups by place of residence
klacksyGroupsAddress.videoLabel: Video: Klacksy forms groups by place of residence
klacksyGroupsAddress.caption: From the addresses, Klacksy builds location groups: region, canton, city and, below them, municipalities — but only where enough people live. Small places are attached to the nearest group. Preview first, applied only after your confirmation. Waiting times are shortened.
klacksyGroupsQualification.title: Groups by qualification
klacksyGroupsQualification.videoLabel: Video: Klacksy forms groups by qualification
klacksyGroupsQualification.caption: Klacksy creates one group per qualification and assigns every employee with a valid qualification — anyone with several is in several groups. Waiting times are shortened.
klacksyGroupsMixed.title: Location and qualification
klacksyGroupsMixed.videoLabel: Video: Klacksy forms qualification groups under a location group
klacksyGroupsMixed.caption: Both combined: under the location group Winterthur, Klacksy forms qualification groups with exactly the people from that region. Waiting times are shortened.
dailyOps.title: Everyday tasks, right in the roster
dailyOps.subtitle: Real recordings from Klacks with demo data: expenses, corrections, replacements and hours, plus the daily timeline with drag & drop — all right in the roster, and the totals update instantly.
containerOps.title: Containers: scheduling tasks within a shift
containerOps.subtitle: Real recordings from Klacks with demo data: a container bundles the tasks of a work shift (such as vehicle check, goods receiving, site inspection, documentation) or forms a tour with route planning. In the roster, a container is scheduled like a normal shift, assigned to one person, and that schedules all of its tasks at once. Fill by drag & drop or automatically, schedule breaks, optimize routes and split between two people.
sporadicOps.title: Special shifts: sporadic, time window, staffing
sporadicOps.subtitle: Real recordings from Klacks with demo data: shifts that only occur occasionally, shifts with a time window, shifts with several employees or several times a day — and shifts that require a qualification. Klacks shows in the roster what is still missing and rejects unsuitable assignments.
scenarioOps.title: Scenarios: planning without risk
scenarioOps.subtitle: Try out variants, check rules and hours live, and only then accept — the original stays unchanged.
expensesDemo.title: Record expenses
expensesDemo.videoLabel: Video: recording expenses on a shift
expensesDemo.caption: Right-click the shift, choose Expenses, enter the amount — the cell shows the amount right away.
correctionDemo.title: Book a correction
correctionDemo.videoLabel: Video: booking a correction on a shift
correctionDemo.caption: The employee stayed 30 minutes longer: Klacks adds a correction block and the hours in the row header update.
replacementDemo.title: Record a replacement
replacementDemo.videoLabel: Video: a colleague takes over part of a shift
replacementDemo.caption: A colleague takes over the last two hours of the shift: both rows show the replacement block and both hour totals update.
hoursAdjustmentDemo.title: Adjust hours
hoursAdjustmentDemo.videoLabel: Video: adjusting the end time of a shift
hoursAdjustmentDemo.caption: Double-click the shift, change the end time in the dialog — duration and totals are recalculated immediately.
timeline24hDemo.title: 24-hour view
timeline24hDemo.videoLabel: Video: roster in the daily timeline view across 24 hours
timeline24hDemo.caption: The roster as a daily timeline across a full 24 hours: you see night and day shifts at a glance.
timelineDayDragDropDemo.title: Shift by drag & drop
timelineDayDragDropDemo.videoLabel: Video: assigning a shift from the shift list to a person by drag & drop
timelineDayDragDropDemo.caption: In the day view, with the visible range from 6 a.m. to 7 p.m., you drag a shift from the shift list onto a person — the shift appears in the roster instantly.
containerFillDemo.title: Fill a container
containerFillDemo.videoLabel: Video: filling a container template with tasks by drag & drop
containerFillDemo.caption: Drag and drop the tasks into the container template — that's how the container comes together in just a few steps.
containerAutofillDemo.title: Fill container automatically
containerAutofillDemo.videoLabel: Video: Klacks fills the container automatically with suitable customer orders
containerAutofillDemo.caption: Klacks fills the container automatically with suitable tasks from the available ones. Here it picks the suitable ones from 10 customer orders with time windows and, since they have addresses, puts them straight into the best order, including the distance — afterwards you print the route as a PDF with a map.
containerPauseDemo.title: Plan a break
containerPauseDemo.videoLabel: Video: dragging a break into a container template and setting the time
containerPauseDemo.caption: Drag a break into the container template and set the time.
containerRouteDemo.title: Optimize route
containerRouteDemo.videoLabel: Video: re-sorting a container with a zigzag route using “Optimize route”
containerRouteDemo.caption: “Optimize route” re-sorts a container with a zigzag route: from 20.9 to 14.8 km. Afterwards you print the route as a PDF with a map.
containerSplitDemo.title: Split a container
containerSplitDemo.videoLabel: Video: splitting a container between two people at a split point between two tasks
containerSplitDemo.caption: You choose a split point between two tasks (no task is cut through) and the person taking over — Klacks splits the container between two people, and you see both halves with their tasks.
shiftSporadicDemo.title: Sporadic shift
shiftSporadicDemo.videoLabel: Video: scheduling a sporadic shift on two days of a week — the remaining days are blocked
shiftSporadicDemo.caption: A sporadic shift only occurs occasionally — here the window cleaning, on at most two days per week. Once it is booked on two days, Klacks blocks the remaining days of that week.
shiftTimeRangeDemo.title: Time-range shift
shiftTimeRangeDemo.videoLabel: Video: scheduling a time-range shift — a start outside the time window is rejected
shiftTimeRangeDemo.caption: A time-range shift applies to a time window (here 08:00–14:00) with a fixed duration. You set the start yourself; if it lies outside the window, Klacks rejects it with a message.
shiftSumEmployeesDemo.title: Several employees per shift
shiftSumEmployeesDemo.videoLabel: Video: a shift that needs three employees — the counter fills from 1/3 to 3/3
shiftSumEmployeesDemo.caption: The stocktaking needs three employees. With each assignment the counter in the roster fills up (1/3, 2/3, 3/3); once the staffing is complete, the day counts as full.
shiftQuantityDemo.title: Shift several times a day
shiftQuantityDemo.videoLabel: Video: a time-range shift that occurs three times a day — each round is scheduled at a different time
shiftQuantityDemo.caption: A patrol round occurs three times a day, 45 minutes each within the time window 08:00–18:00. You set the start of each round yourself (here 08:30, 12:30 and 16:00); the counter shows how many have already been assigned (1/3, 2/3, 3/3). Unlike a shift with several employees, the rounds take place at different times.
shiftQualificationDemo.title: Required qualification
shiftQualificationDemo.videoLabel: Video: a shift with a required qualification — without the forklift licence the assignment is rejected
shiftQualificationDemo.caption: The forklift assignment requires the forklift licence. With the licence the assignment works; anyone who does not have it cannot be assigned to the shift — Klacks rejects the assignment with an error message.
scenarioCreateDemo.title: Create a scenario
scenarioCreateDemo.videoLabel: Video: creating a scenario and moving a shift inside it — the original roster stays unchanged
scenarioCreateDemo.caption: In a scenario you can change the roster without risk. ‘To Original’ shows the unchanged plan at any time.
scenarioAutoWizardDemo.title: Klacks plans as a scenario
scenarioAutoWizardDemo.videoLabel: Video: the AutoWizard plans a week as a scenario — only your approval applies the plan
scenarioAutoWizardDemo.caption: The AutoWizard first plans only inside the scenario (time-lapse). The real roster stays empty until you accept the result.
scenarioCompareDemo.title: Compare variants
scenarioCompareDemo.videoLabel: Video: switching between two plan variants and the original, then rejecting them
scenarioCompareDemo.caption: Switch between variant A, variant B and the original — without touching the real roster.
scenarioRuleDemo.title: Rule violation stays in the scenario
scenarioRuleDemo.videoLabel: Video: a rule violation in the scenario shows up in the error list only there
scenarioRuleDemo.caption: A rest period that is too short is flagged right away in the scenario. Nothing appears in the original roster.
scenarioOps.klacksyHint: Klacksy also creates scenarios and plans inside them — tell it in the chat, for example: “Plan Winterthur from November 2 to 8.”
dailyOps.klacksyHint: Klacksy, the built-in AI assistant, can also do all of this for you on request — for example, tell it in the chat: “Add expenses of 24.50 for Mia on October 6.”
ruleSettings.title: It all comes down to the settings
ruleSettings.subtitle: Klacks offers countless ways to calculate rules and hour credits for nights, weekends, public holidays and overtime — exactly the way your contracts and company agreements require.
ruleSettings.nightWeekend.title: Nights and weekends
ruleSettings.nightWeekend.text: You set the night window and the surcharge rates yourself, and choose up to three weekend days — as a multiplier, a fixed amount per hour or per shift, with an optional minimum per hour.
ruleSettings.holidayOvertime.title: Public holidays and overtime
ruleSettings.holidayOvertime.text: A separate public-holiday rate, and overtime per day or per week in up to three tiers. When several surcharges fall on the same hour, the highest one applies — or all of them add up.
ruleSettings.macro.title: Your own calculation with a macro
ruleSettings.macro.text: If that is not enough, a macro does the maths: a short script using weekday, time of day, public holidays and contract values — with conditions, loops and functions of your own.
ruleSettings.planningRules.title: Scheduling rules
ruleSettings.planningRules.text: Rest periods, maximum daily and weekly hours, consecutive working days, free Sundays or hour caps per period — each one as a warning or as a block.
ruleSettings.klacksyHint: Klacksy helps you get it right in every one of these cases: describe your rule in the chat in your own words, for example “Sundays earn a 50% surcharge.” — Klacksy asks follow-up questions, shows a preview and only saves once you confirm.
